text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
VJESNIK
- Zlatko Aleksovksi, a Bosnian Croat war crimes suspect extradited to the International criminal tribunal by Croatia, pleaded not guilty to charges against him..
- No international agreement binds Croatia to build a Zagreb-Split highway through the Bosnian territory, says Reconstruction Minister Jure Radic.

- Some 122 Serb families now living in Eastern Slavonia have so far applied for return to their old homes in Croatia's former rebel Serb enclaves under the government's new plan for the return of refugees.

- Croatian embassy in Italy refutes allegations made in an autobiography by Italian Felice Manieri, a convicted criminal, about his business connections with President Franjo Tudjman's son, and that he supplied Croatia with heavy weapons.
- A new Croatian-Slovenian agreement on joint management of the nuclear plant Krsko should be ready by July 1, says Zeljko Lalic, the economy minister's assistant for energy.

- Total workforce shrank by 30,000 between 1993 and 1997, but the number of artisans and self-employed grew by 57,000. The sector now represents 13.2 percent in the total workforce, compared to nine percent five years ago.

- The law on areas of special national concern passed by the government a year ago has so far failed to boost settlement of former Serb lands, and most towns are still glaring empty despite promises of better salaries and working conditions.
VECERNJI LIST
- Privatisation authorities envisage some eight to ten investment funds being set up to manage the assets obtained by beneficeries of mass privatisation.

- The industrial output growth trend slowed down in the first quarter of 1997 and is likely to stagnate in April, according to research centre City Trust. It expects a reversal in May with the output growing a monthly 0.43 percent, or 5.3 percent annually.

- Since Sweden's Ericsson gained a majority stake in electronic manufacturer Nikola Tesla, the Croatian firm's sales rose roughly 40 percent to some 250 million German marks in 1996, says its director Per Olof Sjoestedt.
- European Union will donate 300,000 ECUs for two projects of infrastructure reconstruction in Eastern Slavonia, says Per Vinther, Euroepan Commission special envoy in Croatia.
- Privatisation fund HFP decides to sell nine firms and real estate on the Adriatic coast that were formerly owned by companies and institutions from Serbia and Montenegro.
- Croatia has made $122 million from NATO peacekeeping force in Bosnia for its logistics costs.
SLOBODNA DALMACIJA
- State oil monopoly INA negotiates a deal with U.S. firm Halliburton on applying the American technology in oil and gas exploration.
- All disputes should soon be resolved, says Foreign Minister Mate Granic after visiting neighbouring Slovenia.
- Money market: Banking liquidity improves and demand for kuna shrinks, but interest rates still hold.
- Early Easter holidays helped tourist performance in March: overnights 71.4 percent higher than in the same month last year. -- Zagreb newsroom, 385-1-4557075
